meta.title: Spanish — Common phrases and expressions
meta.subtitle: 400 expressions · both directions, as two cards each
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Spanish → English (see the Spanish, recall the meaning) and English → Spanish (see an English meaning, recall the Spanish). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising an expression and producing it are learnt separately. 400 set expressions of Spanish — a string of words whose meaning is not the sum of its parts, which the six DELE level decks teach only where their own word lists happen to name one. There is no published list of the expressions a learner should know, so the candidates are every multi-word entry in the Spanish Wiktionary — a dictionary gives a string of words an entry only when it is an expression in its own right — and which of them are common is measured by counting each one in a corpus of everyday sentences rather than asserted. The cards are ordered roughly by how common the word is in everyday Spanish, so the words you will meet most often come first: the order is taken from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles, with a reflexive verb placed by the verb it is formed from and a phrase, which a list of single words cannot see, placed by how often it turns up in a corpus of everyday sentences. Every noun carries its article, so the gender is learnt with the word (6 of them), and its plural sits directly beneath it; a noun beginning with a stressed a- is given the el it takes in the singular and the las it takes in the plural (el agua, las aguas). Each of the 3 verbs carries its full conjugation: the non-finite forms, all five simple tenses of the indicative, the present, both imperfects and the future of the subjunctive, and the imperative in both its affirmative and its negative. Six persons are shown, from yo to ellos; the Rioplatense vos is not. Compound tenses are formed with haber and the past participle, which is given. Real example sentences come with 398 of the 400 words, up to three apiece, chosen where possible to show three different inflected forms rather than the same one three times, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside it; the sentence corpus has nothing at all for the remaining 2, which are kept because the word list is set by the exam board and not by the corpus. Expressions: the multi-word entries of the English Wiktionary's Spanish, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Ordering and the count of each: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR, which also supplies the example sentences.
